nodes.description: CV pre-catalytic treatment (capacitive region only) in 1.0 M KOH, 0.925-1.025 V vs RHE, 100 cycles
nodes.source_text: CV treatment in 1.0 M KOH electrolyte for 100 cycles using the ZIF-67@CFP electrode. Within 0.1, the ZIF-67@CFP electrode shows a typical capacitor behavior where the non-Faradic charge/discharge currents increase from the first to 60th cycles and stabilize thereafter.

nodes.description: CV pre-catalytic treatment with Co²⁺/Co³⁺ redox in 1.0 M KOH, 0.925-1.325 V vs RHE, 100 cycles
nodes.source_text: At a wider potential window of 0.4... two recognizable redox couples (marked as region I and II) with half-wave potentials (E1/2) at 1.049 and 1.124 V evolve until the 40th cycle... at the 40th cycle, anodic: 0.537 A g⁻¹; cathodic: 0.411 A g⁻¹... total anodic charge reaches 9.80 mC (1.02×10⁻⁴ mmol of Co²⁺), which is merely 1.3% of the total Co²⁺

nodes.description: CV pre-catalytic treatment with full Co redox + OER in 1.0 M KOH, 0.925-1.525 V vs RHE, 100 cycles
nodes.source_text: The lowest overpotential for a current density of 1 A g⁻¹ is 205 mV after 15 cycles. The declining trend of TOF at an overpotential of 296 mV shows that the normalized activity of Co sites decreases from 0.59 s⁻¹ (after 3 cycles) to 0.06 s⁻¹ (after 100 cycles) with a 90% activity loss.

nodes.description: Amperometric OER pretreatment in 1.0 M KOH at multiple potentials, 1h duration
nodes.source_text: OER overpotential at 10 A g⁻¹ decreases from 341 mV (pretreated at 1.025 V) to 300 mV (pretreated at 1.325 V) with Tafel slope increasing from 78.6 to 99.4 mV dec⁻¹... the TOF (overpotential = 300 mV,) maintains at ca. 0.24 s⁻¹... drops to 0.043 s⁻¹ after pretreatment for 3,600 s... BET surface area declines from 932 m² g⁻¹ to 158 m² g⁻¹ after 1h treatment at 1.525 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cubic ZIF-67 nanocubes with mean edge length of 158 nm evenly coated on carbon fiber paper surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: cubic ZIF-67 is obtained following an established method with a mean edge length of 158 nm (Figure 1B). The ZIF-67-modified carbon fiber paper (ZIF-67@CFP) electrode shows evenly coated ZIF-67 nanocubes on the carbon fiber surface (Figure 1C).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show single ZIF-67 nanocube with no clear crystalline structure; featureless SAED patterns rule out other Co-based structures; elemental mappings show uniform Co, N, O distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopic (TEM) image (Figure 1D) and the high-resolution images of selected regions (Figures 1E, 1F, and 1G showing center, corner, and edge regions) imply no clear crystalline structure of ZIF-67, also indicated by the featureless selected area electron diffraction (SAED) patterns.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine ZIF-67 shows characteristic peaks at 7.4° and 12.8° for (011) and (112) facets respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3A, the ex situ X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) pattern of pristine ZIF-67 matches well with the previous report, where two intensive peaks at 7.4° and 12.8° are assigned to (011) and (112) facets, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p3/2 peaks at 780.5, 782.1, 786.1 eV confirm all Co species as Co²⁺; surface N-to-Co atomic ratio of 3.63; O 1s shows physisorbed H₂O (532.9 eV) and OH⁻ (531.7 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pristine ZIF-67 shows a surface N-to-Co atomic ratio of 3.63 ... three peaks at 780.5, 782.1, and 786.1 eV. The former two peaks are ascribed to the surface Co species coordinated with OH- and mIM linkers ... both physisorbed H₂O (532.9 eV) and OH- (531.7 eV) exist on the surface of pristine ZIF-67.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine ZIF-67 has BET surface area of 932 m²/g with sub-2 nm pores matching theoretical 1.7 nm pore size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the BET surface area of ZIF-67 declines dramatically during amperometry, from 932 m² g⁻¹ to 158 m² g⁻¹ after 1h treatment at 1.525 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: At 0.925 V, shows tetrahedral Co sites triplet peaks at 540, 566, 587 nm and minor α-Co(OH)₂ peak at 620 nm; absence of octahedral Co peaks at 480, 506 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At 0.925 V ... the three main peaks at 540, 566, and 587 nm are known as the spinorbital coupling triplet peaks, which can be assigned to the ⁴A₂(F) to ⁴T₁(P) transition of tetrahedral Co sites. The absence of any peaks at 480 and 506 nm rules out the existence of any octahedral Co coordination in ZIF-67.

nodes.characterization_summary: Characteristic peaks at 162, 179 cm⁻¹ (N-Co-N deformation); 266, 687 cm⁻¹ (C-CH₃ stretching); minor α-Co(OH)₂ Eg mode at 629 cm⁻¹ and peak at 522 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The characteristic Raman peaks of ZIF-67 at 162 and 179 cm⁻¹ are attributed to the nitrogen-cobalt-nitrogen (N-Co-N) deformation vibration modes, and the peaks at 266 and 687 cm⁻¹ to the C-CH₃ stretching of mIM linker molecules. At 0.925 V, the minor peak at 629 cm⁻¹ is assigned to the Eg vibration mode of α-Co(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mappings on dark-field TEM image show uniformly distributed Co, N, and O elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mappings on a dark-field TEM image (Figure 1H) suggest uniformly distributed Co, N, and O.
